blocks.content: A Judge of the Supreme Court or the Comptroller and Auditor General can only be removed from office by an order of the President passed after an address by each House of Parliament supported by a special majority.

rows: Presidential order following a Special Majority address in Parliament (Proved misbehaviour/incapacity)
Presidential order after inquiry by Supreme Court under Article 317 (Misbehaviour)
Presidential order after Special Majority address in Parliament
Same grounds and parliamentary procedure as a Supreme Court Judge

items: Distinguish carefully between Parliamentary Address removal (CAG, CEC, SC/HC Judges) and Supreme Court Inquiry removal (UPSC members under Article 317).
Remember the critical age distinction: High Court Judges retire at 62 years, whereas Supreme Court Judges, CAG, and CEC retire at 65 years.
Note that resignation letters for all key constitutional offices must be addressed to the President, not to their respective department or ministry.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Constitutional functionaries like CAG, CEC, and UPSC members hold office for a tenure of 6 years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
Resignations of major constitutional postholders must be submitted in writing directly to the President of India.
Removal of CAG, CEC, and Supreme Court judges requires a special majority in Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
UPSC Chairman and members are removed by the President following a mandatory Supreme Court reference inquiry under Article 317.
High Court judges hold office until 62 years of age, whereas Supreme Court judges serve until 65 years.
